Praised by Lenin as a 'most valuable and major theorist' of the Communist Party, this Bolshevik wrote Imperialism and World Economy in 1915 before being purged in 1937 — who is he?
Nikolai Bukharin: Soviet revolutionary and politician (1888–1938)
This Gabonese politician became president in 1967 and ruled until his death in 2009, surviving even after public pressure forced him to allow multi-party politics in 1990 — who was he?
Omar Bongo: President of Gabon from 1967 to 2009.
The main executive leader of France's Directory regime from 1795 to 1799, this politician steered the country through the later years of the Revolution — who is he?
Paul Barras: French politician, nobleman and military officer (1755-1829)
Serving two non-consecutive terms as Canada's 15th prime minister, this Quebec-born academic co-founded the journal Cité Libre before entering politics via the Liberal Party — who is he?
Pierre Trudeau: Prime Minister of Canada (1968–1979; 1980–1984)
Educated at Sandhurst in England, this man returned home in 1966 and ruled for nearly half a century, becoming the longest-serving leader in the Arab world at his death — which sultan?
Qaboos bin Said: Sultan of Oman from 1970 to 2020.

Modeled on a notorious wave of Revolutionary France violence, this campaign of political repression and mass executions was carried out by the Bolshevik secret police during the Russian Civil War — what is it called?
Red Terror: Bolshevik campaign of political repression and executions (1918–1922)
The first Philippine president from Mindanao and the oldest to take office at 71, this former Davao City mayor led the country from 2016 — who is it?
Rodrigo Duterte: President of the Philippines from 2016 to 2022.
The oldest daughter of her husband's own uncle, this woman was the wife of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein and mother to sons Uday and Qusay — who is she?
Sajida Talfah: First wife of Saddam Hussein.

This wave of mass production, standardization, and rapid scientific discovery, sometimes dubbed the Technological era, is generally dated between 1870 and the outbreak of World War I in 1914. What period was this?
Second Industrial Revolution: 1870–1914 electrical and chemical era.
A writer who governed Tokyo from 1999 to 2012, this prominent ultranationalist was widely criticized for xenophobic and racist remarks against Chinese and Koreans in Japan — who was he?
Across religions this immortal, immaterial essence goes by many names — atman in Hinduism, jiva in Jainism, ruh in Islam — but what's its common English term?
Soul: In religion and philosophy, immaterial essence of a living being.
A 19th-century Muslim reformer and educationist in British India, he's widely credited as the father of the two-nation theory that underpinned the Pakistan movement — which figure was he?
Syed Ahmad Khan: Indian reformer and social activist (1817–1898)

Published by Anton LaVey in 1969, this text serves as the foundational scripture of a philosophy whose adherents describe themselves as 'atheistic' believers who see supernatural figures as projections of personality — which book?
The Satanic Bible: 1969 religious text of LaVeyan Satanism.

Political scientists call it the extreme edge of authoritarianism: a system that seizes both public and private life and rules through nonstop state-media propaganda — what is this form of government?
Totalitarianism: Extreme form of authoritarianism and a theoretical concept.
The only woman ever to serve as chief minister of Rajasthan, this Indian politician also held two Cabinet posts under Atal Bihari Vajpayee — who is she?

Vasundhara Raje: 11th Chief Minister of Rajasthan. Vasundhara Raje Scindia (born 8 March 1953) is an Indian politician, who has held the position of the chief minister of Rajasthan from 2003 to 2008 and 2013 to 2018.
According to medieval European legend, this immortal man taunted Jesus on the way to the Crucifixion and was cursed to roam the Earth until the Second Coming — who is this legendary figure?
The last president to have served in the Civil War — the only one to start as an enlisted man — he led the U.S. through the Spanish-American War before his 1901 assassination; which president was he?
William McKinley: President of the United States from 1897 to 1901.

Commonly known by a compass-direction nickname, this state existed from 1962 until unifying with its southern neighbor in 1990, having been formed when officers toppled a monarchy and sparked an eight-year civil war — which country?
Yemen Arab Republic: Country in West Asia (1962–1990)
A pharmacist by training and MP for Manisa since 2011, which Turkish politician has led the Republican People's Party since 2023?
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Anna Atkins (born 1799) is the earliest of the four. Anna Atkins (née Children; 16 March 1799 – 9 June 1871) was an English botanist and photographer.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below was established earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
John Tyndall is a physicist. John Tyndall (2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Fritz Haber is a chemist. For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
What is the atomic number of Aluminium?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
In what year was Pavel Durov born?
Pavel Durov: Pavel Valeryevich Durov (Russian: Павел Валерьевич Дуров; born 10 October 1984) is a technology entrepreneur.
In what year was Alexander Fleming born?
Alexander Fleming: Sir Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 – 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
In what year was Satya Nadella born?
Satya Nadella: Satya Narayana Nadella (born 19 August 1967) is an Indian-American business executive.
In what year did Sergei Korolev die?
Sergei Korolev: Originally trained as an aircraft designer, Korolev became a leading figure in Soviet rocketry.
In what year did Max Born die?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
In which country is St. Bernard?

St. Bernard (dog breed): Switzerland. The hospice, built by and named after the Alpine monk Saint Bernard of Menthon, 
acquired its first dogs between 1660 and 1670.
Who is credited with discovering General relativity?
General relativity: Albert Einstein. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Who is credited with discovering Tetracycline?
Tetracycline: Lloyd Conover. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Who is credited with discovering Potassium?
Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
Sharing the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics with Martin Ryle for the discovery of pulsars, which British radio astronomer had already earned the Royal Astronomical Society's Eddington Medal in 1969?

Antony Hewish (11 May 1924 - 13 September 2021) was a British radio astronomer who won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1974 (together with fellow radio-astronomer Martin Ryle) for his role in the discovery of pulsars.

This term describes a statement accepted as self-evidently true, serving as a starting premise for further logical reasoning, derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy' — what is it?
Axiom is a statement that is taken to be true, to serve as a premise or starting point for further reasoning and arguments.

Known only from larval and juvenile specimens until video footage of much larger adults surfaced, this deep-sea cephalopod genus holds its long, elbow-like arms perpendicular to its body — what is it?
Bigfin squid are a group of rarely seen cephalopods with a distinctive morphology.
Despite being fully Turing-complete, this minimalist 1993 esoteric language allows only eight commands and takes its unusual name from a slang term for utter confusion — what language is it?
Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Mller.
This Italian mastiff breed once hunted big game and herded cattle, and today mostly serves as a guard dog and loyal companion — name the breed?
Cane Corso is an Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
Famous for color-shifting camouflage and zygodactylous, pincer-like feet, which family of roughly 200 Old World lizard species is this?
Chameleon (family Chamaeleonidae) are a distinctive and highly specialized clade of Old World lizards with 200 species described as of June 2015.
Living in a symbiotic partnership with sea anemones that shelter them from predators, these Indo-Pacific reef fish live in groups led by a dominant breeding female. What fish are they?
Clownfish (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.

This cosmopolitan bird family includes crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, and its roughly 135 species are known for remarkable intelligence, including self-awareness demonstrated in mirror tests — what's the family?
Corvidae is a cosmopolitan family of oscine passerine birds that contains the crows, ravens, rooks, magpies, jackdaws, jays, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers.
This computer scientist, who died in October 2011, partnered with Ken Thompson to build Unix and also devised the C and B programming languages — who is he?

This hypothetical megastructure would encircle an entire star to capture most of its energy output, conceived as a thought experiment for how an advanced civilization might meet growing power needs — what's the concept called?
Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

Native only to a single island in French Polynesia, this arum-family plant is now one of the world's most popular houseplants, and an ecologically damaging invasive species from South Africa to the Pacific Islands. Name it?
Epipremnum aureum is a species in the arum family Araceae, native to Mo'orea in the Society Islands of French Polynesia.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and has been called the 'last universal genius' — who is he?
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was German polymath (1646–1716).

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.
Behaviorally and physically dog-like despite being closer kin to felines, this carnivoran's family is the fifth-smallest in its order with only four extant species — what is it?
Hyena (hi-; from Ancient Greek, haina) are feliform carnivoran mammals belonging to the family Hyaenidae (Latin).
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.
Two years after unveiling the first mechanical television system, this Scottish engineer achieved the first-ever transatlantic television transmission in 1928 — who is he?
John Logie Baird (13 August 1888 - 14 June 1946) was a Scottish inventor, electrical engineer and innovator who demonstrated the world's first mechanical television system on 26 January 1926.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.
Its dust-like, fuzzy, colored appearance on food comes from spores, and its tubular branching network of hyphae counts as a single organism — what fungal structure is it?
Mold (US, PH) or mould (UK, CW) is one of the structures that certain fungi can form.
The paranasal sinuses all drain into this air-filled space that channels inhaled air from the nostrils down toward the throat — what is it?
Nasal cavity is an air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.
This flowering plant genus's name traces to a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco, borrowed via French — which South American garden favorite is it?
Petunia is a genus of 20 species of flowering plants of South American origin.
Emerging roughly 203 million years ago and wiped out alongside the dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this order of long-necked marine reptiles ruled Jurassic seas — what were they?
Plesiosaur are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.

Found below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male reproductive gland acts as a mechanical switch between urination and ejaculation, and produces fluid that becomes part of semen — name the gland?
Prostate is an accessory gland of the male reproductive system and a muscle-driven mechanical switch between urination and ejaculation.
This transhumanist inventor who pioneered text-to-speech and OCR technology later won the $500,000 Lemelson-MIT Prize in 2001 for his work on artificial intelligence — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil (born February 12, 1948) is an American computer scientist, author, entrepreneur, futurist, and inventor.
Born in 1858, this German inventor devised a compression-ignition engine so significant that it and its fuel now both carry his surname — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel (18 March 1858 - 29 September 1913) was a German inventor and mechanical engineer.
This bodily fluid carries reproductive cells along with fructose and enzymes that help them survive their journey toward an egg — name the fluid?
Semen is a bodily fluid that contains spermatozoa from the male gonads of animals.

With the formula NaNO3 and historically mined in massive deposits in Chile, this white, deliquescent salt is a key industrial source used to make fertilizers, pyrotechnics, and explosives — which compound?
Sodium nitrate is the chemical compound with the formula NaNO3. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
A Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist who co-founded New Left Review, this thinker became a founding figure of the Birmingham School of Cultural Studies — who was he?
Stuart Hall (cultural theorist) (3 February 1932 - 10 February 2014) was a Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist, cultural theorist, and political activist.
This American actress won an Oscar, three BAFTAs, two Tonys, and two Emmys, one of only 24 performers ever to complete acting's Triple Crown. Who is she?
Terry Gou (pinyin: Gu Timng; Peh-e-j: Koeh Ti-bng; born 18 October 1950) is a Taiwanese billionaire businessman and politician.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
Neither an insect nor a parasite despite its common name, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few of its kind to have colonized dry land, likely since the late Paleozoic — what is it?
Woodlouse are terrestrial isopods in the suborder Oniscidea.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.

Multicellular eukaryotes that breathe oxygen and grow from a hollow ball of cells called a blastula, over 1.5 million species in this kingdom have been described by scientists. What are they collectively called?
Animal: Biological kingdom. Over 1.5 million living animal species have been described, of which around 1.05 million are insects, over 85,000 are molluscs, and around 65,000 are vertebrates.
Native to alpine lakes and polar coastal waters, this cold-water relative of salmon holds the title of the world's most northerly freshwater fish — what is it?
A cousin of the tomato and potato, this European nightshade is so toxic — via atropine and scopolamine — that even handling it can harm you; its other common name is "belladonna." What's the plant?
Atropa bella-donna: Deadly nightshade, a flowering plant.

Nicknamed the 'stone' or 'house' version of its family, this adaptable mustelid outcompetes its forest-specialist, pine-dwelling cousin in open habitats — and has even gone feral in North America. Which species is it?
Beech marten: Species of carnivore. It is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List on account of its wide distribution, its large population, and its presence in a number of protected areas.
Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, this astronomical body is so compact that not even light can escape past its event horizon. What is it?
Black hole: Compact astronomical body. A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.

This rare and potentially fatal illness comes from a toxin better known by its cosmetic nickname; it starts with blurry vision and slurred speech but usually spares both fever and consciousness — what is it?
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
Tetravalent and able to form four covalent bonds, this element known since antiquity ranks as the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass — which one is it?
Carbon: Chemical element with atomic number 6 (C)

Greek for "head-feet," fishers nickname these inkfish for their ink-squirting trick; their arms are muscular hydrostats modified from the primitive molluscan foot. Which marine class includes the octopus, squid, and nautilus?
Cephalopod: Class of mollusks. The study of cephalopods is a branch of malacology known as teuthology.
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
A tropane alkaloid drawn from the leaves of South American coca plants, it once served doctors as a local anesthetic with handy vasoconstricting properties — what is this stimulant?

Cocaine: Tropane alkaloid and stimulant drug. The leaves are processed into cocaine paste, a crude mixture of coca alkaloids, from which cocaine base is isolated and then converted to cocaine hydrochloride.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.

Named after a mythological Greek youth transformed into a tree after killing his pet stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is found across warm temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Cupressus: Several genera of evergreen conifers.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
Credited as the first to create a transuranium element — neptunium — this Berkeley physicist shared the 1951 Nobel in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Also called Human Factors Engineering, this discipline applies psychology and physiology to reduce errors and boost safety in system design — what field?
Ergonomics: Designing systems to suit their users.
One of only two living species in its genus, this rodent was such a prized delicacy to the ancient Romans that its common name literally advertises the fact. What animal is it?
European edible dormouse: Species of rodent.
When fibroblasts overproduce collagen after repeated injury or chronic inflammation, this permanent connective-tissue scarring can impair an organ's normal function — what is it called?
Fibrosis: Excess connective tissue in healing.
Known for wood used in tool handles, electric guitars, and Morgan Motor Company's sports car frames, this tree genus produced nymphs called the Meliae in Greek myth — which genus?
Fraxinus: Genus of plants. The genus is widespread throughout much of Europe, Asia, and North America.
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is prized smoked as Finnan haddie or the Arbroath smokie — what fish is it?
Haddock: Species of fish. The haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.

Extracted from a Central African plant sacred to Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this hallucinogenic alkaloid was once marketed in Europe as a stimulant before being studied for other therapeutic uses — what is it?
Ibogaine: Psychoactive substance found in plants in the family Apocynaceae.

A theoretical physicist who studied under Max Born earned a chemistry degree from Harvard before pivoting to nuclear physics — and later oversaw the first atomic weapons during WWII. Who is this pivotal figure in physics history?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: American theoretical physicist (1904–1967)
In a landmark 1913 Columbia University address, this American psychologist championed behaviorism and later became known for the unsettling 'Little Albert' experiment — who is he?
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Also called the Mediterranean black widow, this venomous spider is common throughout the Mediterranean region and central Asia — what species is it?

Latrodectus tredecimguttatus: Species of spider. Latrodectus tredecimguttatus, also known as the Mediterranean black widow or the European black widow, is a species in the genus Latrodectus of the widow spiders.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
Able to breathe air thanks to lobed fins and a well-developed internal skeleton, these freshwater vertebrates are considered the closest living relatives of land animals — what are they?
With horn-shaped fins on its head and one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish, this filter-feeding giant may even recognize itself in a mirror — which creature?

Element 101, first made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, was the first that couldn't be produced by simply neutron-blasting a lighter element — and it honors the father of the periodic table. Which element is it?
Mendelevium: Chemical element with atomic number 101 (Md)
This Russian polymath discovered the atmosphere of Venus and formulated the law of conservation of mass, while also helping shape the modern Russian literary language as a poet — who is he?
With roughly 200 species across 16 genera, this family of elongated fish is almost exclusively marine, with a name traced back through Portuguese and Latin to a Greek word — which family?
Moray eel: Family of fishes. Moray eels, or Muraenidae, are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Sold under the brand name Revia, this medication blocks opioid receptors to reduce cravings in alcohol and opioid use disorders and is combined with bupropion to treat obesity — what is it?
Naltrexone: Medication. It has also been found to be effective for the treatment of other addictions and may be used for them off-label.
Discovered in 1846 by Ascanio Sobrero, this oily explosive liquid became the key ingredient in dynamite — what is it?

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
Harvested from Penicillium moulds and brewed in deep tanks, this β-lactam was among the first medicines to knock out staph and strep infections. What is it?
Penicillin: Group of antibiotics derived from fungi.

So reactive that it never appears uncombined in nature, this element was famously isolated in 1669 by Hennig Brand — the scientific community's first documented discovery of an element — and comes in white and red forms. Which one is it?
Phosphorus: Chemical element with atomic number 15 (P)
With a half-life of just 138 days, this rare radioactive element occurs only in trace amounts within uranium ore and is chemically similar to selenium — what is it?
Polonium: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
Encompassing peaches, cherries, plums, and almonds, this genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the rose family produces stone fruits called drupes — which genus?
Prunus: Genus of trees and shrubs.
Botanically a kin of spinach rather than a true grass, this protein-rich Andean pseudocereal was first cultivated near Lake Titicaca thousands of years ago — what is it?
Quinoa: Edible plant in the family Amaranthaceae.
Typically striking two to four weeks after a strep throat, this inflammatory disease can attack the heart, joints, skin and brain — and may permanently scar the heart valves. What is it?
Native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka, this tiny feline is one of the smallest members of its family, and has been listed as Near Threatened since 2016 due to deforestation — which species?
Rusty-spotted cat: Small wild cat species native to South Asia.
This genus contains most of the world's familiar bushy-tailed tree squirrels, found across North America, Europe, temperate Asia, and Central and South America — which genus?
Native to East Asia, this cultivated mushroom is also known as the black mushroom or Chinese mushroom — name the fungus?

Native to Eurasia and found in Paleolithic-era deposits in ancient Britain, this flowering plant's ripe berries and cooked leaves are eaten in some regions despite its nightshade family's fearsome reputation — what is it?
Solanum nigrum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The plant was known and mentioned by ancient herbalists, including Dioscorides.
Known by the Reddit username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded the platform and also launched the now-defunct airfare search engine Hipmunk — who is he?
Steve Huffman: American web developer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Serving as prime minister of Turkey seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, he was also the first PM to have been born in the Turkish Republic — who was he?

Süleyman Demirel: President of Turkey from 1993 to 2000. Demirel was the leader of the opposition from 1971 to 1975 before forming a right-wing government known as the First Nationalist Front, which collapsed in 1977.
With more than 8,000 species known for their loud mating calls and leaf-like camouflage, this insect family also goes by the common name katydids or bush crickets — which family?
Tettigoniidae: Family of insects. Insects in the family Tettigoniidae are commonly called katydids (especially in North America) or bush crickets.
